For `npm` users, this happens if you enabled `ignore-scripts`. 

What worked for me:
```bash
# Remove current version
npm uninstall -g opencode-ai

# Install a working version if you don't trust postinstall scripts
npm i -g opencode-ai@1.15.0
# Or install the latest one 
npm i -g --ignore-scripts=false opencode-ai

# Update to latest allowing postinstall scripts
npm update -g --ignore-scripts=false opencode-ai
```

Additionally, you can disable opencode autoupdate so it doesn't break next time:
```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "autoupdate": "notify"
}
```

There is another problem:

## False “no progress” auto-pause stopped goal continuation prematurely

### Summary

When a session had an **active goal**, `autoContinueGoal` could incorrectly decide that a synthetic continuation turn made **no progress**, immediately set the goal to `paused`, and **stop injecting further continuation prompts**. From the user’s perspective, the agent “stopped on its own” or `/goal resume` appeared to do nothing (goal went back to `paused` within ~200ms).

This was **not** an LLM/provider failure. The goal loop exited before a new LLM turn was enqueued.

### Root cause

After a synthetic goal-continuation user message (`Continue working toward the active session goal.`), auto-pause only inspected the **latest assistant message**. Pure text responses (e.g. a status summary asking “need to continue?”) do **not** count as progress — only tools/patches/subtasks do:

```288:295:packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts
    const assistantMadeGoalProgress = (message: MessageV2.WithParts) =>
      message.info.role === "assistant" &&
      message.parts.some((part) => {
        if (part.type === "patch" || part.type === "subtask") return true
        if (part.type !== "tool") return false
        if (part.tool === "get_goal") return false
        return part.state.status === "completed" || part.state.status === "running" || part.state.status === "pending"
      })
```

**Original buggy condition** (simplified):

```typescript
// BEFORE fix — only looked at the latest assistant
if (
  isGoalContinuationMessage(latestUser) &&
  latestAssistant.finish &&
  !assistantMadeGoalProgress(latestAssistant)  // ← too narrow
) {
  await goals.update({ sessionID, status: "paused" })
  return
}
```

### Failure scenario

Typical message sequence:

1. Synthetic user: `Continue working toward the active session goal.`
2. Assistant A: runs `bash` / other tools (**real progress**)
3. Assistant B (latest): text-only summary, e.g. `## Status summary… need to continue?`

On idle, `autoContinueGoal` (or `/goal resume` → `continueGoal`) saw:

- Latest user = old synthetic continuation message
- Latest assistant = B (text only) → `assistantMadeGoalProgress === false`

So it logged `auto_pause_no_progress` and paused the goal — **even though assistant A in the same stretch had already used tools**.

Observed in logs:

```
goal.continue reason=start
goal.continue reason=auto_pause_no_progress latestAssistantProgress=false
goal.status from=active to=paused
```

No `inject_synthetic_prompt`, no new LLM call.

### Why normal chat still worked

A real user message creates a new turn and does not hit this auto-pause branch the same way. The bug specifically affected the **goal idle-continuation loop**, not arbitrary user prompts.

### Fix

Treat a continuation stretch as “no progress” only if **none of the last N messages** (N=5) contain tool/patch/subtask progress:

```391:405:packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts
        if (
          Option.isSome(latestUser) &&
          Option.isSome(latestAssistant) &&
          latestAssistant.value.info.role === "assistant" &&
          isGoalContinuationMessage(latestUser.value) &&
          latestUser.value.info.id < latestAssistant.value.info.id &&
          latestAssistant.value.info.finish &&
          !recentProgress
        ) {
          yield* goalContinueLog(sessionID, "auto_pause_no_progress", messageContext)
          yield* goals.update({ sessionID, status: "paused" }).pipe(
            Effect.catchIf(NotFoundError.isInstance, () => Effect.void),
            Effect.ignore,
          )
          return
        }
```

Where `recentProgress` is derived from the last 5 messages:

```297:298:packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts
    const recentMessagesMadeGoalProgress = (messages: MessageV2.WithParts[]) =>
      messages.some((message) => assistantMadeGoalProgress(message))
```

I have a more concrete repro shape for the parent/subagent waiting part of this issue, from a sanitized local log on OpenCode 1.15.7.

This happened with a subagent child session on an OpenAI model. The upstream stream emitted a wrapped overload error:

```text
service=llm providerID=openai modelID=<openai_model> session.id=<child_session> agent=<subagent_agent> mode=subagent error={"error":{"type":"error","sequence_number":2,"error":{"type":"service_unavailable_error","code":"server_is_overloaded","message":"Our servers are currently overloaded. Please try again later."}}} stream error
```

The important sequence was:

```text
T+00:00 child session created (version=1.15.7)
T+00:53 service=llm ... code=server_is_overloaded ... stream error
T+00:53 session.prompt cancel
T+30:00 session.prompt cancel
T+30:00 fallback child session created with the same parent/title on a fallback OpenAI model
```

So in this observed case, the child did not visibly remain in retry for 30 minutes. Instead, the child stream failed and the child session moved through the cancel path, but the parent/sync task did not receive a clean terminal failure/completion signal. It waited until the 30-minute inactivity window and then created a fallback child session.

That makes the user-visible behavior slightly different from a pure infinite retry loop:

1. wrapped provider stream error arrives
2. child session is cancelled/idled
3. parent/subagent waiter is not resolved with a terminal failure
4. parent appears hung until the sync inactivity window expires
5. fallback child is created later

No local paths, project paths, API keys, request IDs, or user content are included here. Session IDs and model names above are intentionally masked.

The useful boundary here might be a post-turn hook that receives a small receipt first, not an unconditional "run arbitrary bash after every changed session" path.

Something like:

`{ dirty_files, changed_paths, branch, exit_reason, tests_run, approval_state }`

Then users can wire commit/index/summarize flows however they want, while the core can keep obviously risky actions like `git push` or networked side effects behind explicit policy.

That would still cover the auto-commit / gitnexus indexing use case, but make the safety boundary easier to reason about. If you want, I'm happy to help pressure-test a minimal hook contract that supports this workflow without normalizing surprise pushes.

FYI - Co-pilot thinks this is a bug. Not sure if its helpful:

> Yes — this looks like a real bug in `opencode`'s Gemini protocol adapter.

> The short version: **`thoughtSignature` is defined in the Gemini wire schema, but it is never actually preserved when opencode parses Gemini responses and then replays prior assistant/tool-call messages back to Gemini.** So when Gemini emits reasoning with a signature and then a tool call, the next request can resend the tool call **without** the required `thought_signature`, which matches your Vertex error.

> The strongest evidence is here:

```typescript name=packages/llm/src/protocols/gemini.ts url=https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/8f7a6c4a0076cf69fb57d8e1add3e47194ee6b45/packages/llm/src/protocols/gemini.ts#L27-L46
const GeminiTextPart = Schema.Struct({
  text: Schema.String,
  thought: Schema.optional(Schema.Boolean),
  thoughtSignature: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
})

const GeminiFunctionCallPart = Schema.Struct({
  functionCall: Schema.Struct({
    name: Schema.String,
    args: Schema.Unknown,
  }),
  thoughtSignature: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
})
```

> But when prior assistant messages are lowered back into Gemini request parts, opencode only sends text/reasoning/tool-call content and **drops any signature field**:

```typescript name=packages/llm/src/protocols/gemini.ts url=https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/8f7a6c4a0076cf69fb57d8e1add3e47194ee6b45/packages/llm/src/protocols/gemini.ts#L184-L218
const lowerToolCall = (part: ToolCallPart) => ({
  functionCall: { name: part.name, args: part.input },
})

...

if (part.type === "reasoning") {
  parts.push({ text: part.text, thought: true })
  continue
}
if (part.type === "tool-call") {
  parts.push(lowerToolCall(part))
  continue
}
```

> That means:

> - the schema **accepts** `thoughtSignature`
> - the stream parser **reads** Gemini parts
> - but the parsed `LLMEvent`s / stored message parts do not carry `thoughtSignature`
> - and later request lowering cannot resend it

> The parser path confirms that signatures are not propagated into common events or message parts:

```typescript name=packages/llm/src/protocols/gemini.ts url=https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/8f7a6c4a0076cf69fb57d8e1add3e47194ee6b45/packages/llm/src/protocols/gemini.ts#L354-L367
for (const part of candidate.content.parts) {
  if ("text" in part && part.text.length > 0) {
    lifecycle = part.thought
      ? Lifecycle.reasoningDelta(lifecycle, events, "reasoning-0", part.text)
      : Lifecycle.textDelta(lifecycle, events, "text-0", part.text)
    continue
  }

  if ("functionCall" in part) {
    const input = part.functionCall.args
    const id = `tool_${nextToolCallId++}`
    lifecycle = Lifecycle.stepStart(lifecycle, events)
    events.push(LLMEvent.toolCall({ id, name: part.functionCall.name, input }))
    hasToolCalls = true
  }
}
```

> No `thoughtSignature` is attached to either:
> - reasoning events
> - tool call events

> And the canonical message schema only has generic metadata/providerMetadata fields, with no Gemini-specific first-class signature preservation:

```typescript name=packages/llm/src/schema/messages.ts url=https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/8f7a6c4a0076cf69fb57d8e1add3e47194ee6b45/packages/llm/src/schema/messages.ts#L83-L100
export const ToolCallPart = Object.assign(
  Schema.Struct({
    type: Schema.Literal("tool-call"),
    id: Schema.String,
    name: Schema.String,
    input: Schema.Unknown,
    providerExecuted: Schema.optional(Schema.Boolean),
    metadata: Schema.optional(Schema.Record(Schema.String, Schema.Unknown)),
    providerMetadata: Schema.optional(ProviderMetadata),
  }).annotate({ identifier: "LLM.Content.ToolCall" }),
```

> So my confidence is **high**: the bug is not that the field is missing from the schema; it's that it is **not propagated through the internal event/message model and therefore not replayed on subsequent Gemini requests**.
